title: The GNRS conjecture for minor-free network flow
decision_reason: Canonical pre-draft fingerprint, current independent scholarly corroboration, thirteen inspected source records, fifteen scope comparisons, separated A64 self-review, exact quantifier checks and rendering/link validation passed. No unresolved matching general resolution claim was located; access and proof-review limits remain explicit.

problem_fingerprint.objects: For every fixed finite simple graph H, all finite connected undirected simple graphs G=(V,E) without H as a minor, and every edge-length assignment ell:E->[0,infinity). Minors allow edge contraction and edge/vertex deletion.
problem_fingerprint.metric: d_ell is shortest-path distance, allowed to be a pseudometric because lengths may vanish. The l1 norm on R^m is the sum of absolute coordinate values.
problem_fingerprint.target: A finite C_H>=1 exists such that every such (G,ell) has an integer m>=1 and a map f:V->R^m with d_ell(u,v)<=||f(u)-f(v)||_1<=C_H d_ell(u,v) for every u,v in V.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: C_H depends only on H, not on the number of vertices, edge lengths or their scale/ratios. The map and finite dimension may depend on (G,ell); zero-distance vertices may have the same image.
problem_fingerprint.flow_formulation: For arbitrary finite nonnegative capacities c on E and nonnegative demands D on unordered distinct vertex pairs, with at least one positive demand, let lambda* be the maximum common fraction of every demand carried by capacity-feasible fractional path flows. Let phi be the minimum across cuts with positive separated demand of total crossing capacity divided by total separated demand. The equivalent target is lambda*>=phi/C_H, for every such instance. Zero-capacity cuts are allowed; the inequality avoids an undefined zero-over-zero gap.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Supply graph is undirected and excludes H. Demand pairs are arbitrary and need not yield a planar combined graph. Flows may split across paths, no integrality or node-capacity constraints. The metric target requires all pairs and purely multiplicative distortion.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One entry includes general minor-free, planar and equivalent fractional flow-cut formulations. No separate count for face-cover, bounded-width or demand-layout restrictions.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Connected finite graphs suffice for the finite-distance formulation. Simple graphs lose no metric examples because parallel edges can be replaced by their minimum length and loops discarded; in the flow formulation parallel capacities can be summed.

statement_sources.locator: Author manuscript October 22, 2002: Introduction pp.2–3; Section 2 pp.4–6; Theorem 3.2 and unnumbered conjecture in Section 3, pp.7–8.
STOC 2009 pp.245–246: metric and flow definitions, Theorem 1.1 and Conjecture 1.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Asks equality of undirected network-coding and fractional-routing throughput regions for all networks. GNRS compares cut upper bounds with fractional routing on minor-free supply graphs; it does not allow coding or seek exact equality.
Seeks a single spanning tree with small usage of every unweighted cut. GNRS embeds all shortest-path distances or routes arbitrary fractional demands; no spanning-tree selection is required.

source_records.title: Improved Upper Bounds for the Directed Flow-Cut Gap
source_records.locator: Introduction Theorems 1–5; Section 2.1 pp.5–6 and Corollary 7.
source_records.read: Read formal directed flow–multicut model, concurrent-flow/sparsest-cut comparison and n^(1/3+o(1)) bounds, including edge/node-capacitated scopes.
source_records.access_limit: Main flow-cut terminology refers to multicut. Concurrent-flow corollary is also size-dependent; no fixed-minor constant follows.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Metrics on graphs of treewidth two embed into ℓ1 with a universal constant.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Treewidth two is a proper restriction; arbitrary H-minor-free graphs and even all planar graphs are not covered.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Bound controlled by the cycle rank |E|-|V|+1.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Cycle rank can grow without bound within planar graphs. It is not the fixed surface-genus parameter.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Fixed-forest exclusion gives constant-distortion stochastic tree embeddings.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The forbidden graph is restricted to a forest; general forbidden minors are not settled.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: General GNRS reduces to its planar case together with a clique-sum embedding assertion.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: An equivalence/reduction does not prove either remaining conjecture.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Improved approximation under a stronger relaxation can exceed the performance implied by the standard flow LP.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: An algorithmic sparsest-cut approximation does not alone bound the maximum-concurrent-flow relaxation gap.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Terminal distortion O(sqrt(log gamma)) for a face cover of size gamma, with the single-face case separately solved; distance lower bounds restricted to terminal pairs.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Gamma may grow with graph size. A constant for a bounded face cover is not a constant for arbitrary terminal placement/all pairs.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Constant fractional flow-cut guarantee when each demanded pair is cofacial in a fixed planar drawing.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Arbitrary demand pairs need not share any face. The embedding lower bound is for the cofacial pairs, not all pairs.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Outerplanar fractional flows can be rounded unsplittably with additive capacity overflow bounded by 2 d_max; a lower-bound example limits such rounding.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Restricts the supply graph and begins with a feasible fractional flow; does not prove arbitrary-planar fractional feasibility from cut bounds.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Congestion rounding assumes strongly uncrossed fractional flows; pairwise-planar demand layouts yield integral flow–multicut comparisons.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Demand layout is restricted, and multicut/value optimization differs from concurrent flow against sparsest cut. Neither the restriction nor the objective difference can be dropped.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Tree flow sparsifiers have polylogarithmic quality, including the improved planar bound.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Quality depends on n and concerns a tree proxy. No size-independent ℓ1 distortion or cut-to-concurrent-flow constant results.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Constant distortion for planar metrics realizable on simply connected Busemann non-positively curved surfaces.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The curvature-realization hypothesis excludes general weighted planar metrics.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Constant directed bounds for restricted graph families, with uniform demands in the series-parallel/bounded-pathwidth statements.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The unrestricted demand/class combination required by GNRS is missing. Asymmetry alone is not the reason for the scope distinction.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Directed planar uniform and nonuniform gaps are O(log² n) and O(log³ n).
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: These grow with graph size; the conjecture asks for a constant.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Constant distortion of minor-free metrics into ℓ∞ with O_(r,epsilon)(log n) coordinates.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Target norm differs. The growing dimension prevents transferring the same constant to ℓ1 by elementary norm comparison.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Directed multicut rounding and concurrent-flow consequences with n^(1/3+o(1)) bounds.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Both the main objective and the size-dependent bound must be distinguished; no general fixed-minor constant is proved.

second_review.arrangement: Primary-agent source research followed by a clearly separated adversarial self-pass after drafting; no independent agent or human review.
issues_found: Flow constraints should be explicit, including arbitrary pairs, fractional splitting and finite capacities.
Zero lengths and zero-capacity cuts can create hidden injectivity or division assumptions.
Cycle rank, strongly uncrossed hypotheses and flow–multicut terminology can be misread.
Constant maximum-norm embeddings and directed restricted-class results have superficially matching titles.
issues_resolved: Added both path-flow inequalities and a common demand multiplier; rendered them on separate aligned lines.
Allowed pseudometrics and used phi/C <= lambda* <= phi instead of an undefined ratio.
Recorded cycle rank rather than genus; retained strongly uncrossed and demand-layout conditions; separated concurrent-flow and multicut objectives.
Read full relevant SSS17, KS21, F25 and BS26 definitions/theorems and recorded the graph, demand, target-norm and size-dependence differences.
second_review.application_check: A topology-dependent comparison between capacity bottleneck certificates and feasible fractional multicommodity throughput. No claim concerning interference, packet deadlines, queueing delay or integral scheduling.
second_review.search_limit: Searches and theorem-scope comparisons neither exhaust all literature nor independently certify the cited proofs.

aliases: bounded flow-cut gap for minor-closed graph families

independent_corroboration.qualification: Chekuri's May 2026 notes explicitly retain the general and planar questions; Alemán Espinosa–Schlomberg independently report the nonconstant planar gap in ICALP 2026. They are distinct author groups. Overlapping teams and multiple versions of a work are not counted as independent corroboration.

normalization_checks: Every fixed excluded finite simple graph H, every finite connected undirected simple supply graph without that minor, and every finite nonnegative edge-length assignment.
One constant depends only on H, independent of graph size and all edge-length ratios. The finite output dimension and map may depend on the instance.
Zero lengths give a pseudometric; the image may identify zero-distance vertices. No injectivity assumption is added.
All vertex pairs receive both metric inequalities. Terminal-only lower bounds do not establish the target.
Capacity-feasible nonnegative path weights meet a common demand multiplier; demands may split and need not be integral. At least one pair has positive demand.
Cut minimization is over cuts of positive separated demand. The inequality lambda* >= phi/C handles zero capacity without an undefined 0/0 ratio.
Demand topology is unrestricted. Fractional concurrent flow/sparsest cut differs from maximum-value flow/multicut and from integral or unsplittable rounding.
Planar, bounded-width and face-cover cases and the equivalent metric and flow formulations constitute one family for counting.
